**Conclusion: yes, with an important qualification.** Human rotavirus susceptibility varies by genotype in relation to host histo-blood-group-antigen traits: secretor status (mainly FUT2) is strongly associated with infection by common P[8] and P[4] strains, while P[6] strains are more often found in nonsecretors. Lewis phenotype (mainly FUT3) has also been associated with genotype-specific susceptibility, but its independent contribution is less consistent and can be difficult to separate from secretor status.

These are population-level associations, not absolute rules: people outside the commonly associated phenotype can still be infected, and findings may differ by population and circulating strains. Also, studies of symptomatic rotavirus disease do not always establish susceptibility to infection itself.

**Evidence limitation:** I attempted literature searches and checked the evidence graph, but the search agent returned no usable citations or study-level results, and the graph contained no relevant records. So this is a qualified conclusion rather than a source-verified review.
